findings.summary: docs/architecture.md section 8 states 'the failure blast radius is wider than the pre-11.2 per-item library read' without quantifying the difference; the concrete change is same-connection serialization/latency, not a larger count of independent failures.

The claim is conservative (overstates rather than understates), so it is not an overclaim. Mirrors 11.4-F1.

findings.summary: The repeatable bulk id list is chunked by OperationalLimits.ReconciliationBatchSize (default 100, validated 1-1000) rather than a dedicated request-line bound, so a user-configured maximal batch can still approach provider request-line limits and fall back to the direct read.

At the default batch of 100 the query string is small; at the maximum of 1000 it is roughly 11 KB. Reusing the library-enumeration batch size as the id-chunk bound couples two unrelated concerns, which is a design smell but not a defect. Tracked as 11.2-F3.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: 1. One provider library read per connection serves a reconciliation window instead of one read per work item.
acceptance_criteria_assessment.assessment: Verified against source and independently-run tests. RadarrMetadataReader.ReadAsync consults ArrInventoryCache.TryGet first and only populations on a miss; PopulateAsync issues one GET /api/v3/movie for the whole library plus one bulk GET /api/v3/moviefile?movieId=... for the movies with a file, then every work item is matched from the cached observations with no provider library read. SonarrMetadataReader is structurally identical (one GET /api/v3/series, one GET /api/v3/episode?seriesId= per series, one bulk GET /api/v3/episodeFile?episodeFileIds= for files the embedded resource does not resolve). ProviderInventoryCacheIntegrationTests proves one /movie request serves two distinct identities with whole-library retention, a second in-window read makes no provider call, the bulk selector URIs replace per-item reads, concurrent cold readers coalesce to one library read through the per-connection single-flight gate, and an over-bound/failed-read population keeps the direct read. Documented nuance (accurate): Sonarr episode enumeration is O(series) per window, not O(1), and a sparse webhook window repopulates the whole library; both are recorded in docs/limitations.md F1 and ADR-018 Consequences.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: 2. Invalidation is ArrTags-side (webhook, Jellyfin library refresh/post-scan, scheduled/manual reconciliation, bounded TTL); no provider conditional request, revision token, or SignalR dependency.
acceptance_criteria_assessment.assessment: Verified. LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync calls InvalidateInventory()/InvalidateAll() after the enabled/fence guards and before enumeration; ArrtagsReconciliationTask (Scheduled, which manual execution reuses), ArrTagsPostScanTask (PostScan), and ConfigurationReconciliationTrigger (PostSave) all route through ReconcileAsync. WebhookIntakeService.ResolveAndEnqueue invalidates the event's provider/connection (resolved via the same ArrConnectionCatalog.FromSnapshot identity the readers use) before enqueuing any hint, with a bounded invalidate-all fallback. ArrInventoryCache.TryGet evicts an expired set, and ArrayInventoryCacheEntry.StaleUntil is the bounded TTL fallback. ReconciliationTriggerTests.ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource covers PostScan/Scheduled/PostSave via served-before/not-served-after, WebhookResolutionTests.ServiceInvalidatesTheEventConnectionInventoryScopedToThatConnection covers per-connection scoping, InventoryCacheInvalidationTests covers the TTL eviction and the no-SignalR assembly guard, and ProviderInventoryCacheIntegrationTests.ProviderReadsUseNoConditionalRequestRevisionTokenOrHistorySinceWatermark pins the endpoint-path and query-key allowlists. Independent grep of src found no If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since/history-since/SignalR (only a Jellyfin source-image ETag used in MediaIdentityFactory, unrelated). The periodic scheduled reconciliation keeps its unchanged 12-hour interval.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: 3. The cache is bounded and secret-free, with validated TTL/size limits.
acceptance_criteria_assessment.assessment: Verified. OperationalLimits gains InventoryCacheTtlMinutes (default 15, validated 1-1440), InventoryCacheMaxRecords (default 10000, validated 1-100000), and InventoryCacheMaxBytes (default 32 MiB, validated 1 MiB-256 MiB), validated at configuration load, cloned into the immutable snapshot, and exposed on the ADR-016 settings page. ArrInventoryCache stores at most one observation set per ArrConnectionId keyed by a secret-free identity (provider kind + normalized base URL; API key and userinfo excluded), rejects an over-bound or scope-invalid set before it displaces a retained one, and is in-memory only (never persisted, rebuilt empty on restart). The only free-text carrier is a bounded ArrProviderError; value-level redaction is the producer contract (documented, consistent with MetadataStateEntry.LastError). ArrInventoryCacheTests (24) covers the bounds, FromLimits binding, secret-free member-type denylist, distinctness from the per-item state, and the TTL boundaries; the 11.1 security review returned PASS_WITH_FINDINGS with 0 open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM.

acceptance_criteria_assessment.criterion: 4. Provider failure keeps the existing bounded last-known-good behavior.
acceptance_criteria_assessment.status: met-at-integration-test-level (under the clarified per-item reading confirmed below)
acceptance_criteria_assessment.assessment: Verified. On a failed cold population the reader returns the bounded ArrMetadataReadResult.Failure and caches nothing (PodulateAsync returns InventoryPopulation.Failed before TryStore in both readers), so the inventory cache never serves a failed read as current. The retained last-known-good is the unchanged per-item MetadataStateEntry path: MetadataReconciliationProcessor.ProcessAsync calls KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale on a Retryable.Later failure, which writes the still-usable entry as explicit Stale via MetadataStateEntry.ToStale() without extending its bounded window; MetadataReconciliationProcessor is untouched by Phase 11 (not present in any of the four task diffs). ProviderInventoryCacheIntegrationTests.RadarrLibraryReadFailureOnACacheMissFailsTheWindowAndKeepsBoundedLastKnownGoodMetadata composes the real reader, real cache, real processor, and real durable MetadataStateStore and asserts the per-item state is Stale with an unchanged fingerprint/ExpiresAt/StaleUntil. Separately, an already-stored observation set is served through the TTL second half without a provider call (RadarrStaleObservationSetIsServedWithoutAProviderCallWhenTheProviderFails), which is the TTL-driven bounded last-known-good, not failure-driven retention.

criterion_4_clarified_reading.reading_under_review: The retained last-known-good is the unchanged per-item MetadataStateEntry path (MetadataReconciliationProcessor.KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale); the inventory cache caches nothing on a failed cold population and is not an inventory stale-serving mechanism on failure.
justification: Source: RadarrMetadataReader.PopulateAsync returns InventoryPopulation.Failed before any TryStore on a library-read failure, and ReadAsync returns the bounded failure when population.Error is set; SonarrMetadataReader is identical. No failure path writes the cache.

Source: the last-known-good behaviour is MetadataReconciliationProcessor.KeepLastKnownGoodAsStale -> MetadataStateEntry.ToStale(), which preserves the entry's fingerprint, ExpiresAt, and StaleUntil; the file is unmodified by Phase 11.
Test: the composed integration test asserts exactly this (Stale per-item state, unchanged fingerprint/ExpiresAt/StaleUntil, empty inventory cache) at the real reader/cache/processor/store boundary.

ADR-018 clause 5's 'existing bounded last-known-good semantics' is therefore correctly read as the pre-existing per-item metadata semantics; the Consequences record that failure-driven inventory retention is not realized, and the inventory's own stale-serving is TTL-second-half, not failure-driven.
Soundness caveat: clause 5's literal wording is still divergent (P11R-F4); the reading is sound but the clause would read more precisely with an optional pointer to the per-item path.

summary: Phase 11 (v1.1 Goal C, ADR-018) is complete and architecturally consistent with GOALS.md, the PLANS.md Phase 11 spec, ADR-018, and the documented data model. All four acceptance criteria are genuinely met at the integration-test level, verified by independent source inspection and an independently reproduced clean build (0 warnings / 0 errors), full suite (Failed 0, Passed 1421, Skipped 63, Total 1484, no new skips), focused Goal C suite (55/55) and invalidation-source tests (42/42). The provider inventory cache is bounded, secret-free, non-authoritative, in-memory, keyed by the secret-free ArrConnectionId, and consumed through one DI singleton by both readers and both invalidation services; one library read per connection plus the bulk file selectors serve a reconciliation window (with the honest Sonarr O(series) and sparse-window bounds recorded); invalidation is ArrTags-side across the complete trigger set with no conditional request, revision token, history/since, or SignalR dependency and the periodic scheduled reconciliation unchanged; and provider failure keeps the unchanged per-item bounded last-known-good MetadataStateEntry while the inventory caches nothing on a failed cold population. The criterion-4 clarified reading (per-item last-known-good; no inventory stale-serving on failure) is SOUND. The sibling Phase 11 review's applicable findings (P11-F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F9) are genuinely addressed or not applicable on this branch, and the two that remain (P11-F7 v1.1.md planning line; P11-F8 phase aggregate) are the same non-blocking deferrals; no sibling finding reveals an unresolved real gap here. All task-level findings are LOW and tracked; there is no BLOCKER or HIGH finding, so the phase is APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS and ready for Phase 12. Closure actions before Gate 11 is formally met: move the v1.1.0-phase11 tag from the sibling commit b852c99 to this branch and remove the sibling worktree (P11R-F2), create docs/implementation/phase-11/orchestration.json (P11R-F1), and reconcile the Gate 11 status lines; the LOW documentation/technical-debt items (P11R-F3/F4/F5/F6/F7/F8/F9/F10) should be carried forward as tracked follow-ups.
